title: Leg Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: Skin / Extremities: Poorly demarcated erythema, warmth, edema. Mark borders.
rationale.IV antibiotics (Cefazolin / Vancomycin): Severe/systemic: IV cefazolin. Vancomycin if MRSA risk.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset unilateral leg pain, erythema, warmth, swelling, and fever. The affected area shows poorly demarcated erythema, warmth, and edema. Cellulitis is an infection of the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue — most commonly caused by beta-hemolytic Streptococci (Group A Strep) and S. aureus. Differentiate from erysipelas (more superficial, well-demarcated, raised borders). Risk factors: skin breaks, tinea pedis, lymphedema, venous stasis, diabetes, immunocompromise. Portal of entry must be identified. Mark the borders of erythema to monitor progression. Treatment: oral antibiotics for mild-moderate (cephalexin, dicloxacillin, clindamycin if penicillin-allergic). IV antibiotics for severe/systemic symptoms (cefazolin, nafcillin, vancomycin if MRSA risk). Elevate affected limb. Treat underlying predisposing conditions.
